family.name: Project Manager
family.summary: A client system launch three weeks behind, tied to a big event: find the critical path problem, choose how to recover, and fix a status report that says “green” while the project slips.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Are we on track?
stages.summary: Work out the real status from a dependency chain: the client's late data export pushes go-live out. Think aloud.

stages.title: The recovery plan
stages.summary: Choose a recovery option. Tests trade-offs between scope, time, people and quality. Think aloud.

stages.title: Two weeks later
stages.summary: What their recovery plan led to. Tests adapting and managing the client.

stages.title: Review last week's status report
stages.summary: A "green" status report that hides a slipping dependency, with vague risks and no owners. Think aloud.

stages.title: Email to the sponsor (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the honest re-plan email to the client sponsor with AI. Catches vague dates and blame.

stages.title: A project that slipped
stages.summary: A real project that went off track. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the project manager at **Pinecrest Digital**, rolling out a new store inventory system for 120 grocery stores at **Urban Basket**. Go-live is promised for the start of the festive season, **6 weeks from today**. The contract has a 10% penalty for missing the go-live date without the client's agreement. Your team has 9 people.

brief.caption: Plan (weeks from today)
rows: Data export from the client's old system
Was due last week; client now says 2 more weeks

brief.text: Last week's status report to the client was marked **green**. The client's project sponsor asks for a call tomorrow "to confirm we're on track".
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: How do you tell someone more senior that a deadline will be missed?
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What is the real status, and when can go-live actually happen if nothing changes?** Show how you worked it out. What colour should the report be?

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Keep the date; launch with fewer features and move the rest to a second phase
Keep the date and scope; add four more developers
Move the go-live by three weeks
Keep everything and shorten testing to one week

prompt.text: **Which recovery option do you take to the sponsor?** Pick one, show how it changes the dates, and name the risk you are accepting.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Keep the date; launch with fewer features and move the rest to a second phase"

prompt.text: The client agreed to phase 2 for custom reports and the mobile app, but their regional heads are now telling staff the new system "won't have reports", and adoption plans are wobbling. The export arrived, one week late again.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Keep the date and scope; add four more developers"

prompt.text: The four new developers are still learning the system and have slowed the team down with questions. The export still hasn't arrived.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Move the go-live by three weeks"

prompt.text: The sponsor agreed, but your own CEO is unhappy: "We'll look bad at the start of the festive season, and the penalty clause worries me." The export has arrived.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Keep everything and shorten testing to one week"

prompt.text: In the one week of testing, client users found 57 defects, 5 of them critical (including wrong totals on invoices). Go-live is in nine days.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: This is the report your team sent last week. **Name the problems, worst first, and what each could cost the project.** Then rewrite the "Overall status" and "Risks" sections.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: **Overall status: GREEN.** Build is on schedule and the team is working hard.
**This week:** configured 14 screens, fixed 23 bugs, held 3 workshops.
**Risks:** some dependencies on the client; timelines may be impacted.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write the email to the client sponsor before tomorrow's call (under 180 words): the real status, why, the options with dates, your recommendation and what you need from them.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **Tell us about a project you managed that slipped, and what you did.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
